items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: So I asked Jimmy Blanton would he like to join us.

ctx.x: heard anyone play a bass like that before in my life. And it so happened that Jimmy Blanton had remembered the time when Alphonso Trent's band had played Chattanooga, he was a little kid, and he heard the Trent band and he was admiring the Trent band that he had heard back a few years before that time.

So I asked Jimmy Blanton would he like to join us. He said, yes, that he thought he'd be happy to. He said, but he wanted to go back home first, he went back home, and he went back to -- He was going to Tennessee State, then he wrote us and said that he was -- he was ready to leave, so we sent for him to come to St. Louis, and we took him down to the music store and he picked out a bass fiddle. We didn't buy it for him, we just stood for it. And that was when he bought his big fiddle.

Every night on the job, man, he was just terrific. He just -- he was just out of this world. So, that summer, getting back to Mugs Roberts, when we decided to go to Chicago and make those recordings Jimmy Blanton was with us during the time and in the personnel of that band that made those recordings there was George Hudson, Crack Stanley and Merle (unintelligible) am I right?
